intro.caption: Lesson 2-9 — mean absolute deviation (MAD). Blink's stunt footage is shaking! Before Dex can blame the floor, Mei measures how far Blink's hover heights stray from the mean.

balloons.t: Blink's footage is wobbling! Five test hovers hit 18, 22, 20, 24, and 16 feet.
I am NOT wobbly! My average height is totally fine!
To measure spread around the mean, we have to find the mean first!
Deviations from 20 are −2, +2, 0, +4, −4. They add to ZERO! Blink has zero wobble!
Signed deviations ALWAYS cancel to zero! Take the ABSOLUTE VALUE so every distance is nonnegative.

pages.caption: A deviation is how far a value is from the mean. Taking the absolute value turns every deviation into a nonnegative distance.

balloons.t: No canceling out! Turn every deviation into a positive distance (or zero) and add them up.
Hey! Go easy on the wrench, Mei!
Do not stop at the sum! Divide by how many values there are to get the MAD.
Smaller MAD means steadier hover! Let's beat that test drone!

pages.ch: Boss Gate · Pick the Steadier Drone

balloons.t: Rotor tightened! Now let's compare MADs and see if Blink is ready to film.
If Blink holds steady, I get to do the mega ramp replay!
MAD down to 0.5 feet! Crisp footage, zero excuses, and Dex is cleared for replay!

win.caption: The mean absolute deviation (MAD) is the average distance of data values from the mean. Smaller MAD means less spread and more consistency.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Find the Mean
gates.prompt: Find the mean of each drone's 5 test hover heights before measuring spread.
hints: Conceptual: MAD measures distance from the mean, so you must find the mean first.
Procedural: add all 5 heights, then divide by 5.

fb.msg: 100 is the sum of the 5 hovers. Divide by 5 to find the mean.
24 is the highest hover, not the mean.
16 is the lowest hover, not the mean.
30 is the sum! Divide by 5 hovers.
5 is how many hovers there are, not the mean height.

gates.pass: Blink's mean is 20 ft and Drone B's is 6 ft. Now let's measure how far they stray!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Absolute Deviations
gates.prompt: Find the nonnegative distance of each hover from the mean — no canceling out!
hints: Conceptual: distance from the mean is never negative. Even a value below the mean adds to the spread.
Procedural: for each value, compute |value − mean|, then add all 5 distances together.

worked.q: What is the absolute deviation of 15 from a mean of 19?

items.label: For 18, 22, 20, 24, 16 (mean 20), sum of all 5 absolute deviations:
items.aria: sum of absolute deviations from 20 for 18, 22, 20, 24, 16

fb.msg: 0 happens when you keep minus signs (−2 + 2 + 0 + 4 − 4)! Use absolute value so all distances are nonnegative.
2.4 is the MAD (after dividing by 5). This box asks for the SUM of the 5 absolute deviations.

items.q: Why do we take the absolute value of each deviation before averaging?

options.t: So negative and positive deviations do not cancel to zero
To turn every deviation into a negative number
options.fb: Absolute value makes every deviation 0 or positive, never negative.

options.t: To delete any value equal to the mean
options.fb: A value equal to the mean has a deviation of 0, and we still keep it in the count!
Absolute value only removes minus signs; it does not double any distance.

gates.pass: Sum of absolute deviations is 12 — zero canceling! Dex puts his zero sign away.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Compute the MAD
gates.prompt: Finish the MAD by dividing the sum of absolute deviations by the total number of values.
hints: Conceptual: MAD is the AVERAGE of the absolute deviations — including any 0s in the count.
Procedural: divide the sum of all absolute deviations by how many data values there are.

worked.q: Sum of absolute deviations is 15 across 5 values. What is the MAD?

items.label: Blink's MAD for 18, 22, 20, 24, 16 (sum of absolute deviations = 12, count = 5):

fb.msg: 12 is the sum of absolute deviations! Don't forget to divide by 5.
Did you divide 12 by 4? Keep the 0 deviation in the count — there are 5 values!
Remember to use absolute values so the deviations don't cancel.

items.fbDefault: Divide the sum of absolute deviations (12) by 5.

items.label: Find the MAD of 4, 9, 7, 10, 5 (mean 7):

fb.msg: 10 is the sum of the absolute deviations (3 + 2 + 0 + 3 + 2). Now divide by 5!
Keep the 0 deviation from 7 in the count: divide 10 by 5, not 4.

items.fbDefault: Find |x − 7| for each value (3, 2, 0, 3, 2), add to 10, and divide by 5.

gates.pass: Blink's MAD is 2.4 ft! Now Mei tightens the rotor for the final test.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Pick the Steadier Drone
gates.prompt: Compare two drones, calculate Blink's post-repair MAD, and explain what MAD = 0 means.
hints: Conceptual: a smaller MAD means data points cluster tightly around the mean (more consistent).
Procedural: find the mean, find each |value − mean|, sum them, and divide by the total count.

worked.q: Data set: 9, 11, 10, 10 (mean 10). Sum of absolute deviations?

items.q: Lock 1 · Drone A and Drone B both have a mean of 20 ft. Drone A's MAD is 0.8 ft and Drone B's MAD is 2.4 ft. Which is steadier?

options.t: Drone B, because a bigger MAD means higher flights
options.fb: A bigger MAD means MORE spread — more wobbling away from 20 ft!

options.t: Both are equally steady because their means match
options.fb: Two data sets can share the same mean (20 ft) and have very different spread!

options.t: Drone A, because a smaller MAD means flights stay closer to the mean
Drone A, because its mean is smaller
options.fb: Both drones have the exact same mean of 20 ft.

items.label: Lock 2 · After repair, Blink's 4 hovers are 19, 21, 20, 20 (mean 20). New MAD:

fb.msg: 2 is the sum of absolute deviations (1 + 1 + 0 + 0). Divide by 4 hovers!
Don't skip the two 0 deviations! Divide 2 by all 4 hovers.

items.q: Lock 3 · What does it mean if a drone's MAD is 0?

options.t: Every hover was at the exact same height, with zero spread
Half the hovers were above the mean and half below
options.fb: Symmetric data can still have a large MAD. Zero MAD means zero distance from the mean.

options.t: The drone never left the ground
options.fb: A drone hovering at 20, 20, 20, 20 has a mean of 20 and a MAD of 0!

options.t: We forgot to take absolute values
options.fb: If every value equals the mean, even the absolute deviations are 0.

gates.pass: 0.5 ft MAD! Blink locks into a rock-steady hover — ready for stunt cam!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-9 — what the wobbly drone taught us
rows: MAD measures spread around the mean, so compute the mean first.
Find |value − mean| for every data point so negative and positive differences do not cancel to 0.
Average the absolute deviations — including any 0s in the total count.
A smaller MAD means the data values cluster closer to the mean (steadier, less spread).
journal.quote: "Wobble is just data asking for a wrench." — Mei

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-9 (Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation) as one focused read. Covers computing MAD in three steps, why absolute value prevents signed deviations from canceling, and comparing spread.
